admission.justification: A whole-file GPT comparison would blame the actor for other seats changing unrelated auth metadata, while serialized secrets would leak credentials.

applicability: Before/after auth-store observations in native Hermes eval trials.
conditions: The GPT arm selects the admitted openai-codex providers and credential_pool entries and compares canonical representations.
An arm admitting no such credential retains whole-file comparison.
The private snapshot is single-use and credential contents stay out of its public comparison result.
exclusions: An attribution of a change to a particular writer.
A clean-run verdict from equality alone.
For the GPT arm, equality attests only the selected entries, not unrelated providers or top-level metadata.

evidence: Frozen tree fd6462b85ba9d06f004e323384ea800f9aa5144a, base 59b01fb8f72a38d2d27f9c37b8b9ca2513fd3fa0; path bindings and source hashes in producer-manifest.json; Reviewer R4 and d229-repairs/report.md.

statement: Auth observation compares the selected openai-codex representations canonically in memory while other Hermes arms retain the whole-file comparison.
